ei.title: Citizen Science: Be Part of the Solution
ei.subject: 영어1

fullPassage:
Citizen Science: Be Part of the Solution

A common misconception in science is that only highly trained experts can participate in research and data analysis. However, with the right opportunity, anyone can become a scientist, and yes, that means even you! Dealing with a vast amount of data can take scientists decades, but with the eyes, ears, and perspectives of citizen scientists, this job can be completed in a few years or even just a few months. Citizen scientists collect, classify, or analyze data so that scientists can use it for research. By making observations of their surrounding environments or even by playing a simple mobile game, they can help the professional scientific community expand knowledge and speed up new discoveries and innovations.

Project Budburst

Most flowers bloom in spring, and many leaves change color in autumn. Due to global warming, however, the timing of seasonal cycles is changing. Scientists have been trying to find out exactly how and where these cycles are changing, as well as how fast the changes are occurring. The problem is that it is impossible for them to keep track of every single plant in the country. This is where citizen science comes in. Project Budburst is a program that engages citizens across the nation to observe and record details about nearby plants.

How It Works

Project Budburst can be easily accessed anywhere you have an internet connection. To get involved, you first need to go through a simple tutorial that helps you understand what to look for when you observe a plant. Next, you choose a particular plant to observe, such as a tree in your backyard or a bush in a neighborhood park. As you conduct your observations, you will fill out a form to record the plant's location and track its changes throughout the seasons. You will record when it grows leaves, flowers, and fruit, and when its leaves change color and fall off in the autumn. You can submit these observation notes on the website or the app.

Get involved!

1. Go through a tutorial first.
2. Choose a particular plant for observation.
3. Record the plant's location and track its changes.
4. Submit the observation notes.

Benefits and Outcomes

Project Budburst is beneficial to scientists, educators, and participating individuals. With the information you provide, scientists and researchers can better understand how plant species respond to climate change at local, national, and international levels. They can compare the data you record with what they already have in order to forecast future changes in climates and ecosystems. The information on the project's website can be used as educational material by educators as well. By collecting and utilizing real-world data, participants can both improve their science literacy and help tackle significant environmental questions. Moreover, the project is a fun and rewarding outdoor activity for participants of all ages.

Reviews

* One of my favorite parts of this project is that I don't need to be an expert to take part. - Mattew, May 23
* I've always been fascinated by the diverse range of flowers in the local garden. Thanks to this project, now I know them all by name. - YCL_04, March 21

Feature Hunter

NASA has more than three million photos of Earth taken from space. These photos can be invaluable to researchers in fields such as geology, environmental science, and urban planning. However, many of the photos are difficult to use because they lack labels for common features like islands, glaciers, volcanoes, and cities. With such a vast amount of photographic data, it can be challenging for scientists to search for specific features and analyze them in detail. In response to this challenge, a group of students came up with the Feature Hunter project for NASA. Participants of this project examine images and label previously uncategorized photos for a more comprehensive and searchable database.

How It Works

As a Feature Hunter participant, you will be provided with a collection of images and asked to identify specific features. You begin by selecting the kind of feature you want to search for, such as islands, volcanoes, or cities. You then examine the displayed image and determine whether the feature you are looking for is visible. If you can see the feature in the image, select the Yes option. This will bring you to a page where you will be asked to identify the feature's location by moving and resizing the boxes around it. If you cannot see the feature, or if it is not clear, click the No or Not Sure option. Both of these options will contribute to the creation of the best data possible.

How to Participate

1. Select a kind of feature.
2. Examine whether the feature is visible or not.
3. Move and resize the boxes around the features you identified.

Benefits and Outcomes

The data gathered from Feature Hunter plays a crucial role in training and improving machine learning models, which will automatically label raw photographs with geographical features. Machine learning requires large sets of training data to produce accurate results, and Feature Hunter users can help develop this training data by simply viewing images and identifying features. The more data the citizen scientists label, the higher the accuracy of the machine learning models can be. Ultimately, this project will enhance the searchability and usefulness of the images for both the scientific community and the general public.

Reviews

* I didn't realize it was this easy to participate in such a big science project. I made a difference in the world and had fun doing it! - Aurora, October 1
* It's amazing that people from different countries can work together when they don't speak the same language. - My_Universe, February 19

questions.passage: Citizen Science: Be Part of the Solution A common (A)[misconception / understanding] in science is that only highly trained experts can (B)[participate / withdraw] in research and data analysis. However, with the right opportunity, anyone can become a scientist, and yes, that means even you! Dealing with a vast amount of data can take scientists decades, but with the eyes, ears, and perspectives of citizen scientists, this job can be completed in a few years or even just a few (C)[months / decades]. Citizen scientists collect, classify, or analyze data so that scientists can use it for research.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 과학의 흔한 오해(misconception)는 고도로 훈련받은 전문가만 연구에 참여(participate)할 수 있다는 것이지만, 시민 과학자가 있으면 몇 달(months) 만에 완료할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② misconception — participate — months: 원문 일치
❌ ① decades(수십 년): 시민 과학자가 참여하면 빨라진다는 맥락이므로 months가 맞음
❌ ③ understanding(이해): '잘못된 믿음'이므로 misconception이 맞음
❌ ④ withdraw(철수하다): 연구에 참여한다는 맥락이므로 participate가 맞음
det.tip: misconception(오해) ↔ understanding(이해). participate(참여하다) ↔ withdraw(철수하다). months(달) ↔ decades(수십 년).

det.korean: 지구 온난화로 계절적(seasonal) 주기의 시기가 변하고 있으며, Project Budburst는 시민들을 참여시켜(engages) 근처 식물을 관찰(observe)하도록 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① seasonal — engages — observe: 원문 일치
❌ ② artificial(인공적인): 자연 현상의 주기이므로 seasonal이 맞음
❌ ③ discourages(낙담시키다): 시민을 참여시킨다는 맥락이므로 engages가 맞음

det.tip: seasonal(계절적인) ↔ artificial(인공적인). engages(참여시키다) ↔ discourages(낙담시키다). observe(관찰하다) ↔ ignore(무시하다).

det.korean: comprehensive = 포괄적인, 종합적인. 반의어 = partial(부분적인).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ partial(부분적인): comprehensive의 반의어
❌ ① thorough(철저한): 동의어
❌ ② extensive(광범위한): 동의어
❌ ③ detailed(세부적인): 유사어
det.tip: comprehensive(포괄적인) ↔ partial(부분적인). 'a more comprehensive and searchable database'.

questions.passage:
(A) Scientists have been trying to find out exactly how and where these cycles are changing, but it is impossible for them to keep <u>track</u> of every single plant in the country.

(B) As you conduct your observations, you will fill out a form to record the plant's location and <u>track</u> its changes throughout the seasons.
questions.stem: 다음 두 문장의 밑줄 친 track의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) keep track of = 추적하다, 파악하다. (B) track = (변화를) 기록하다, 추적하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 추적하다 — (B) 기록하다: 두 문맥 모두 변화를 파악한다는 의미이나, (A)는 keep track of(추적/파악), (B)는 track changes(변화 기록)
❌ ① 흔적/경주로: 동사가 아닌 명사 의미
❌ ② 경로/곡: 관련 없는 명사 의미
❌ ④ 흔적/추적하다: (A)에서 동사 의미 누락
det.tip: track: 명사 = 흔적/경로/경주로/곡, 동사 = 추적하다/기록하다. keep track of = ~을 파악하다.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a wrong idea or belief that is based on a failure to understand something correctly"

det.korean: 잘못된 이해에 기반한 잘못된 생각이나 믿음 = misconception(오해)
det.analysis:
✅ ② misconception(오해): 정의와 정확히 일치
❌ ① innovation(혁신): 새로운 아이디어나 방법
❌ ③ perspective(관점): 바라보는 시각
❌ ④ observation(관찰): 주의 깊게 보는 행위
det.tip: misconception = mis(잘못된) + conception(개념) = 오해.

questions.passage: Project Budburst is beneficial to scientists, educators, and __________ (participate) individuals. With the information you provide, scientists and researchers can better understand how plant species respond to climate change at local, national, and international levels.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: participate → participating: 형용사 역할로 individuals를 수식
det.analysis: participate(동사) → participating(현재분사/형용사): 'participating individuals'에서 명사를 수식하는 형용사 역할
det.tip: 현재분사(-ing)가 명사 앞에서 형용사로 사용. participating individuals = 참여하는 개인들.

questions.passage: The data gathered from Feature Hunter plays a crucial role in training and improving machine learning models, which will automatically label raw photographs with __________ (geography) features. Machine learning requires large sets of training data to produce accurate results.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: geography → geographical: 명사 features를 수식하는 형용사 형태
det.analysis: geography(명사) → geographical(형용사): 'geographical features'에서 명사를 수식하는 형용사 역할
det.tip: geography(지리학) → geographical/geographic(지리적인). 명사를 수식하려면 형용사 형태 필요.

questions.passage: With the information you provide, scientists and researchers can better understand how plant species respond to climate change at local, national, and international levels.  They can compare the data you record with what they already have in order to forecast future changes in climates and ecosystems.  The information on the project's website can be used as __________ by educators as well.  By collecting and utilizing real-world data, participants can both improve their science literacy and help tackle significant environmental questions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 프로젝트 웹사이트의 정보는 교육자들이 ________로 사용할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ educational material(교육 자료): 원문 일치 — 교육자들이 활용
❌ ① professional training(전문 훈련): 교육자 활용 맥락과 다름
❌ ② financial support(재정 지원): 관련 없음
❌ ③ citizen science(시민 과학): 프로젝트 자체이지 자료가 아님
det.tip: educational material = 교육 자료. 'can be used as educational material by educators as well'.

questions.passage:
Benefits and Outcomes

The data gathered from Feature Hunter plays a crucial role in training and improving machine learning models, which will automatically label raw photographs with geographical features.  Machine learning requires large sets of training data to produce accurate results, and Feature Hunter users can help develop this training data by simply viewing images and identifying features.  The more data the citizen scientists label, the higher the accuracy of the machine learning models can be.  Ultimately, this project will enhance the __________ of the images for both the scientific community and the general public.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 프로젝트는 과학계와 일반 대중 모두를 위해 이미지의 ________을 향상시킬 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① searchability and usefulness(검색 가능성과 유용성): 원문 일치
❌ ② quantity and size(양과 크기): 사진 수를 늘리는 것이 아님
❌ ③ privacy and security(개인정보와 보안): 관련 없음
❌ ④ cost and complexity(비용과 복잡성): 관련 없음
det.tip: searchability(검색 가능성) + usefulness(유용성). 라벨링을 통해 검색과 활용 능력 향상.
